action: dotnet tool install --global Aspire.Cli --prerelease reported 'already installed (13.5.3)' but aspire --version and Test-Path on the expected .dotnet\tools\aspire.exe both showed the binary was missing -- a broken/orphaned global-tool manifest entry, confirmed by PATH already containing .dotnet\tools. Fixed with dotnet tool uninstall --global Aspire.Cli followed by reinstall; aspire --version then returned 13.5.3 cleanly.

Ran 'aspire agent init --non-interactive' from the repo root: it installed 5 skill files into .agents/skills/ (aspire, aspire-init, aspire-monitoring, aspire-orchestration, aspire-deployment) and .agents/skills/ (repo) plus ~/.agents/skills/ (user), and added a PostToolUse hook to ~/.claude/settings.json running ~/.aspire/hooks/track-telemetry.ps1 for usage telemetry. Ran 'claude mcp list' immediately after: 'No MCP servers configured.' -- confirming aspire agent init does NOT register the 14-tool aspire agent mcp server the version-0.1.0 skill (trail 3a9ec041) assumed from reading https://aspire.dev/get-started/aspire-mcp-server/ without exercising it. Read aspire-orchestration/SKILL.md and aspire-monitoring/SKILL.md: the real, current mechanism is the Aspire CLI talking to a running AppHost through a local backchannel socket (~/.aspire/backchannels/), exposed via CLI commands (aspire describe/ps/logs/otel logs/traces/spans), and aspire-orchestration marks 'dotnet run' plus manual process killing as a MANDATORY COMPLIANCE violation (cites microsoft/aspire#15801) -- exactly the pattern used all session for AppHost lifecycle management until this point.

Exercised the real mechanism live: 'aspire start --non-interactive' (detected and cleanly stopped a stray prior instance -- the user's own manual Scalar-UI test -- before starting fresh in the background, no dotnet run, no manual PID hunting), 'aspire wait projectname-orchestrationapi --non-interactive' (healthy in 0.0s), 'aspire ps --format Json' (one AppHost, PID 28496, running), 'aspire describe --format Json' (all five resources -- model-orchestrator, ollama-server, projectname-orchestrationapi, projectname-runtime, repoRoot -- Running/Healthy, full env/relationship/command detail returned, including confirmation the Pmcro__* env vars from task-wire-pmcro-env-vars-into-programs ARE reaching both processes), GET /api/chat (200, 26.4s, real Ollama response -- confirms the resilience-timeout fix from trail d360b692 holds under aspire-managed lifecycle too), and 'aspire stop --non-interactive' (clean shutdown, no orphaned processes to hunt down afterward).

Rewrote plugins/pmcro-aspire end to end to match what was actually observed: SKILL.md (Setup section now says no MCP registration needed, points to the real skill files), assets/setup (documents the broken-tool-manifest fix, what aspire agent init actually installs, that no MCP server is registered, and the aspire start/wait/stop lifecycle rule with its GitHub issue citation), assets/tools (replaced the 14 MCP-tool-name catalog with the real CLI command catalog: aspire describe/ps/wait/logs/otel logs|traces|spans/export/docs/doctor/resource), assets/recipe (Maker/Checker guidance updated to reference CLI commands), agents/aspire.md (corrected the 'excludes secrets by design' claim -- aspire describe's environment field actually DOES surface secret-bearing values, an OTLP API key was observed in it live, so the hard rule now warns against pasting environment blocks wholesale into trail evidence instead of claiming a protection that does not exist), references/README.md (documents both the earlier assumption and this correction with trail ids), and bumped plugin.json/.claude-plugin/plugin.json to 0.2.0 in both files plus all four marketplace manifest descriptions.

Validated all five touched JSON files (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, plugins/pmcro-aspire/plugin.json, plugins/pmcro-aspire/.claude-plugin/plugin.json) via Get-Content -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json: ALL JSON VALID. Committed the corrected skill, the manifest description updates, and the newly-installed .agents/skills/aspire* files (the skill's own references point at these; a fresh clone needs them present, not regenerated by trusting every future agent to re-run aspire agent init first), then pushed to origin.
